definition: API Versioning is a core concept in .NET Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What API Versioning is
theory.body: API Versioning describes the methods and patterns used within .NET Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: API Versioning is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why API Versioning matters
theory.body: Without API Versioning, systems built with .NET Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How API Versioning works
theory.body: The mechanism behind API Versioning follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of API Versioning.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of API Versioning
theory.body: API Versioning offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
